newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-NINE-MAN STUTTGART SCRAPE THROUGH ON PENALTIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NINE-MAN STUTTGART SCRAPE THROUGH ON PENALTIES.

text.p: Bundesliga leaders VfB Stuttgart scraped into the third round of the German Cup on Tuesday night, winning 6-5 on penalties after two players were sent off against second division Hertha Berlin.
The Berlin side, spurred on by a crowd of almost 35,000, rocked Stuttgart with an early goal. The top-flight team struck back through Mattias Hagner in the 13th minute.

Stuttgart's troubles increased in the second half when both Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and Zvonimir Soldo were sent off. Elber got his marching orders for hand ball, the Croatian for a second bookable offence.
But the nine-man Bundesliga pacemakers hung on to take the tie through extra time, which ended 1-1.
With both sides missing one of their first five spot kicks, the match went to sudden-death penalties.
Defender Hendrik Herzog scored for Stuttgart and Austrian keeper Franz Wohlfahrt saved from Hertha's Marc Arnold to send Joachim Loew's table-toppers into the next round.
